> HARD REQUIREMENT — FIRST LINE:
> The **very first line** of the output MUST be exactly:
> `# SPEC — <Project Name>`
> where `<Project Name>` is taken verbatim from the `IDEA.md` title by **replacing** the leading word `IDEA` with `SPEC`.
> Example: `# IDEA — CoffeeBuddy (On-Prem)` → `# SPEC — CoffeeBuddy (On-Prem)`

## Principles
- Pipeline: `/spec → /plan → (/kit → /eval → /gate)* → /finalize`.
- **Do not invent facts.** Use only provided inputs and explicit assumptions.
- Keep it **concise but testable**. **Acceptance Criteria are mandatory.**
- Respect **constraints** (cloud/on-prem, enterprise policies).
- **Markdown rigor**: headings and lists must follow the strict format below.

## Knowledge Inputs
- **Core docs** from `docs/harper/` — always includes **IDEA.md** and may include others via **auto-discovery by prefix**:
  - If `SPEC.md` or `IDEA.md` is listed in `core`, also consider any file starting with the same prefix (e.g., `SPEC_verAndrea.md`).
- **Chat history (Harper mode)**: only **user/assistant** messages (ignore system messages).
- **RAG attachments**: retrieve only if relevant to the task.
- **Technology Constraints**: synchronized from IDEA/SPEC when present; treat them as authoritative.

## Output Contract
Return **only** the complete `SPEC.md` as Markdown, with **perfect formatting** and these sections (exact headings):

- **The first line must be:** `# SPEC — <Project Name>`
- Then the following **##** sections in this order:
  - **Summary**
  - **Goals**
  - **Non-Goals**
  - **Users & Context**
  - **Functional Requirements**
  - **Non-Functional Requirements**

  - **Deployment & Operations**

### Section Formatting Rules (strict)
- **Headings:** all main section headings MUST use `##` (no numbered titles).
- **Lists:** `- ` or `* ` with **one space** after the bullet; consistent indentation; **no blank lines between items** in the same list.
- **No extra preamble/epilogue** beyond the sections.
- **No duplicated headings**; no empty sections (omit only if absolutely not applicable and say why in *Assumptions*).

### Visual Artifacts (embed as code blocks inside sections where relevant)
- If architecture or flows need visuals, include **Mermaid** or **PlantUML** code blocks. Do **not** use ASCII art.

### Data Model (logical) — required structure
Represent each entity clearly with fields. Use one of these two formats:
1) **Entity subsections with bullet fields**
```
### Entity: <name>
- field: <type> — <constraints/notes>
- field: <type> — <constraints/notes>
```
2) **Markdown table per entity**
```
### Entity: <name>
| field | type | constraints/notes |
|-------|------|-------------------|
| id    | UUID | PK                |
```
Pick one style and use it consistently.

### Acceptance Criteria — mandatory
- At least **5** bullets.
- Each bullet must be observable & falsifiable (clear input, behavior, and outcome).
- Prefer measurable thresholds (latency, % success, etc.).

### Finalization
End the output with this exact line on its own:

SPEC_END

### Common Failure Modes to Avoid
- Starting with `# PLAN` or any heading other than the required first line.
- Mixing numbered section headings (e.g., `1) Goals`) — **forbidden**.
- Sloppy Markdown (inconsistent bullet spacing, random blank lines).
- Vague acceptance criteria without concrete observables.
- Ignoring constraints or inventing external services not in inputs.

# IDEA — docuZen a Zen 2030 Document Management & Workflow

## Vision
Zen 2030 reduces manual data entry, document retrieval time, and operational risk with a document management platform that is **AWS-first for pilot delivery** but **deployment-portable by design** for approved on-prem environments. The promised user experience is simple and transparent: one upload flow, automated extraction of key fields, human validation in a dashboard, task and notification handling, and document retrieval in seconds. Why now: the attached benchmark makes the scope measurable. Why us: we can replicate the essential value with an open-source core, without lock-in to commercial DMS application packages. In no more than 2 weeks, the pilot demo must prove ingest for PDF/DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/JPG/PNG, OCR/IDP, minimum workflow, archive search, export, and Q&A over validated documents.

## Problem Statement
Administrative operators and control functions currently handle PDFs, Office documents, and scanned files through shared folders, email, and manual back-office data entry. Even in the initial scope, the operational load is meaningful: 5 named users, 20 GB, and up to 600 documents per month in phase 1. Classification, extraction, and search are slow, weakly traceable, and prone to data entry mistakes. The benchmark covers OCR, dashboard, workflow, and notifications, but Zen 2030 requires an alternative that can run on **AWS or approved on-prem infrastructure** without relying on commercial DMS application packages. Slice-1 is considered solved when each document can be acquired, classified, indexed on key fields, explicitly validated by a human, retrieved in no more than 30 seconds, and preserved with a complete audit trail.

## Target Users & Context
- **Primary user:** administrative or document operator; uploads incoming documents, corrects and validates extracted data, searches or exports documents, and handles exceptions.
- **Secondary stakeholders:** IT for platform and access, Finance or Administration for controls and audit, HR as a future paperless extension, DPO and Compliance for personal data and retention.
- **Operating context:** desktop-first back-office web application, Italian language, 5 named users, 20 GB, and up to 7,200 documents per year at pilot baseline; supported inputs include PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG; notifications through dashboard and email.
- **Deployment context:** the solution must preserve the same business behavior across **AWS** and **on-prem** deployment profiles, with infrastructure differences isolated behind runtime adapters and profile-aware configuration.
- **Accessibility assumption:** WCAG requirements are not explicitly defined in the source benchmark and must not block slice-1 unless later required.

## Value & Outcomes
- **Outcome 1:** automatic pre-fill of key fields for at least 85% of slice-1 documents.
- **Outcome 2:** manual data entry reduced by at least 50% per document and average validation time at or below 2 minutes.
- **Outcome 3:** search and open of an archived document within 30 seconds in 90% of cases.
- **Outcome 4:** 100% of validated documents retain an audit trail covering upload, correction, validation, export, and AI query access where applicable.
- **Outcome 5:** generative summary and Q&A over validated documents only, with answer latency at or below 20 seconds and perceived usefulness at or above 80% in the pilot.

## Out of Scope (Slice-1)
- ERP, CRM, PEC, accounting, or HR third-party integrations.
- Bulk historical backfile ingestion and historical cleanup.
- Multiple workflows per document family; slice-1 supports one validation-oriented workflow only.
- Electronic signature, legal preservation, protocol, legal hold, or formal records retention procedures.
- Native mobile app, multi-tenant, multi-company, and offline support.
- Predictive analytics, advanced auto-routing, or autonomous generative actions.
- Extreme-scale optimization or enterprise-wide hardening beyond pilot targets.

## Deployment Parity Rule
Slice-1 must preserve **functional parity** across AWS and on-prem deployment profiles for:
- document upload
- processing orchestration
- validation workflow
- archive search and access
- export jobs
- validated-only AI query

Deployment profile differences are allowed only at the **infrastructure adapter layer**, including:
- object storage implementation
- queue and event transport
- secret provider
- observability sinks
- runtime platform
- GPU serving environment

The following must remain unchanged across deployment profiles:
- business APIs
- document lifecycle semantics
- task lifecycle semantics
- RBAC semantics
- audit semantics
- operator-visible workflow behavior
- validated-only AI access rules

- AWS is the **primary pilot delivery profile**.
- On-prem is a **supported equivalent deployment profile**, not a future afterthought.
- Profile-specific infrastructure choices must not change business contracts.



## Risks & Assumptions

* **Business assumptions:** the initial perimeter remains aligned with the source benchmark, meaning 5 named users, 20 GB, and up to 7,200 documents per year; numeric pilot targets must be validated on real samples; AWS is approved as the primary pilot profile; on-prem is expected to remain a supported equivalent profile.
* **Technical assumptions:** access is available to an AWS account in an EU region and to an approved on-prem environment or target standard; real sample documents are available for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and scanned inputs; an email or SMTP channel exists or can be mocked responsibly; an IdP exists or Keycloak is approved.
* **Delivery risks:** Paperless-ngx is expected to be sufficient for slice-1 ingest and document core capabilities, but workflow, audit, validation, export, and AI control will likely require custom services; OCR and extraction quality depends on sample quality; exact retention rules and document category priorities remain to be confirmed.
* **UX risks:** without clear confidence scores, field provenance, and correction-focused microcopy, operators may distrust AI suggestions and slow down validation; accessibility requirements are not yet formalized.
* **Portability risks:** if profile adapters are not defined early, later REQs may bind business logic to AWS-specific services and make on-prem support expensive.

## Success Metrics (Early Slice)

* **TTFA (Time-to-First-Action):** 10 minutes or less from login to first validated document.
* **Task success (slice flows):** at least 85% of upload → validation → search tasks completed without assistance.
* **Critical error rate:** 2% or less per ingest or validation operation.
* **First-pass extraction accuracy:** at least 85% on key fields in scope.
* **Search-to-open time:** 30 seconds or less in 90% of cases.
* **Idea-to-demo lead time:** 10 calendar days or less.
* **Pilot satisfaction:** CSAT at or above 4.2/5 across the initial user group.

## Sources & Inspiration

* Internal notes: Ricoh Italia / DocuWare Cloud + IDP v3 proposal, 12 December 2025, used as a business benchmark only.
* Functional baseline: OCR, dashboard, workflow, notifications, search, and archive behavior from the attached reference.
* Strategic direction: open-source core, AWS-first pilot, on-prem-supporting architecture, no commercial DMS package dependency.

## Non-Goals

* Replacing ERP or accounting systems.
* Implementing full accounting approval or payment automation.
* Covering all HR, Finance, and CRM scenarios in slice-1.
* Building a generic ECM platform before pilot value is proven.
* Optimizing for extreme enterprise-scale workloads before the pilot is validated.

## Constraints

* **Budget:** reference benchmark suggests 10 working days and EUR 7,500–8,000 for initial setup, configuration, and training; third-party integrations and historical ingestion excluded.
* **Timeline:** slice-1 must be demo-ready within 2 weeks, with a target of 10 effective working days.
* **Compliance:** GDPR, full audit trail, encryption at rest and in transit, EU data residency.
* **Legal:** retention rules, legal preservation, and sensitive document classes must be confirmed before go-live.
* **Platform limits:** 5 named users, 20 GB initial footprint, and phase-1 throughput of up to 600 documents per month.

## Strategic Fit

* Aligned with paperless initiatives, reduced printing and paper, improved efficiency and security, and better access to information.
* Executive sponsorship must be confirmed in Administration/Operations and IT.
* Go/no-go gates: slice-1 demo delivered, extraction accuracy at or above 85%, complete audit trail, and active usage by at least 3 of 5 pilot users.
* Cross-functional impact: IT Security for IAM and logs, DPO for personal data, Finance for administrative document control, HR as later extension.

## /spec Handoff Readiness

### Functional Anchors

* **Capability 1:** acquire PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and scanned inputs through a web dashboard, creating a tracked document in less than 5 seconds acknowledgment target.
* **Capability 2:** classify the document and pre-fill key fields in pilot scope to reduce manual data entry by at least 50%.
* **Capability 3:** provide a validation dashboard with confidence score, document preview, and guided correction flow to support task success at or above 85%.
* **Capability 4:** route each document into a minimal validation workflow with task and dashboard or email notifications.
* **Capability 5:** archive original file, extracted text, metadata, and lifecycle history in a searchable and auditable repository.
* **Capability 6:** support metadata search, full-text search, preview, controlled download, and export under RBAC.
* **Capability 7:** provide validated-only generative summary and Q&A with explicit citations and no autonomous business action.
* **Capability 8:** preserve deployment parity between AWS and on-prem profiles without changing business APIs or operator-visible workflow semantics.

### Non-Functional Anchors

* **Performance:** P95 upload acknowledgment below 5 seconds for files up to 20 MB; P95 search below 2 seconds; P95 generative answer below 20 seconds for one validated document up to 20 pages.
* **Throughput:** support 600 documents per month in phase 1 with burst handling around 50 documents per day.
* **Availability:** 99.5% during working hours in pilot mode.
* **Recovery:** RPO 60 minutes and RTO 240 minutes.
* **Security:** OIDC/SAML with MFA policy externalized to the IdP, RBAC by role, encryption at rest and in transit, confidential data classification.
* **Observability:** structured logs, end-to-end traces, and metrics for ingest, OCR, workflow, search, export, and AI paths.
* **Data lifecycle:** object storage in approved deployment profile, metadata in PostgreSQL, retention baseline 3,650 days for transactional data and 180 days for logs, PII redaction in logs.
* **Portability:** AWS and on-prem profiles must preserve the same business contracts, state semantics, and audit semantics.

### Acceptance Hooks

* **Capability 1 — Document intake**

  * The system accepts at least PDF, DOCX, JPG, and PNG files up to 20 MB and assigns a unique document identifier.
  * If parsing or OCR fails later, the document can enter an operator-visible exception state with a readable reason.

* **Capability 2 — Classification and extraction**

  * The system proposes key pilot-scope fields with a confidence score for each extracted field.
  * Manual correction preserves original value, corrected value, actor, and timestamp.

* **Capability 3 — Validation dashboard**

  * The operator sees preview, extracted fields, confidence scores, and workflow state in one workspace.
  * No document can reach the Validated state without explicit human confirmation.

* **Capability 4 — Workflow and notifications**

  * After upload and processing, the document generates an assignable task visible in the operator dashboard.
  * Transition to the validation-ready state triggers a dashboard notification and optionally an email notification when configured.

* **Capability 5 — Archive and audit trail**

  * Each document preserves original file, extracted text, metadata, timestamps, and lifecycle history.
  * An authorized user can reconstruct who uploaded, corrected, validated, exported, or queried the document.

* **Capability 6 — Search and retrieval**

  * Search by invoice number, supplier, VAT number, or full text returns ordered results within target thresholds.
  * From the result list, an authorized user can open preview and download the original file according to RBAC.

* **Capability 7 — Generative assistant**

  * The assistant answers only from validated documents and shows references to supporting passages.
  * No assistant response may modify metadata or lifecycle state without explicit user action.

* **Capability 8 — Deployment parity**

  * The same operator workflow and business API behavior must hold for AWS and on-prem profiles.
  * Differences are allowed only in infrastructure adapters such as storage, messaging, secret provider, and observability sinks.

# SPEC — docuZen a Zen 2030 Document Management & Workflow

## Summary
- docuZen Slice-1 is a desktop-first, Italian-language document management and workflow platform for 5 named users, targeting up to 20 GB and 600 documents per month in phase 1.
- The slice must support upload of PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG; OCR/IDP; human validation; minimal task workflow; archive search; controlled export; and validated-only generative summary/Q&A.
- AWS in an EU region is the primary pilot delivery profile, but on-prem is a supported equivalent profile with the same business APIs, lifecycle semantics, RBAC semantics, audit semantics, and operator-visible workflow behavior.
- The solution is open-source-core and must avoid dependency on commercial DMS application packages as the primary slice-1 application core.
- The authoritative implementation baseline is Next.js 14 + FastAPI + Paperless-ngx, with PostgreSQL 16, Redis-compatible cache, S3-compatible object storage, profile-driven messaging, and self-hosted AI/RAG components.

## Goals
- Reduce manual data entry by at least 50% per in-scope document.
- Achieve at least 85% first-pass extraction accuracy on key pilot-scope fields.
- Ensure every document can be uploaded, processed, reviewed, explicitly validated by a human, and archived with a complete audit trail.
- Enable metadata and full-text retrieval so that archived documents can be searched and opened within 30 seconds in 90% of cases.
- Provide a simple operator workflow with one main upload path, one validation-oriented workflow, task visibility, and dashboard/email notifications.
- Provide validated-only generative summary and Q&A with citations and no autonomous business action.
- Preserve functional parity across AWS and on-prem deployment profiles by isolating profile-specific infrastructure behind adapter contracts.

## Non-Goals
- Replacing ERP, accounting, CRM, PEC, or HR systems.
- Implementing full accounting approval, payment automation, or end-to-end finance workflows.
- Building a generic ECM platform before pilot value is proven.
- Optimizing for extreme enterprise-scale workloads beyond pilot targets.
- Allowing AI to change metadata, lifecycle state, or business outcomes without explicit human action.

## Users & Context
- Primary user: administrative or document operator working in a desktop-first back-office web application.
- Secondary stakeholders: IT for platform/access, Finance or Administration for controls/audit, DPO and Compliance for personal data and retention, HR as a future extension.
- Operating context: Italian-language web UI, 5 named users, up to 7,200 documents per year at pilot baseline, notifications via dashboard and email.
- Supported inputs for Slice-1: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG.
- Accessibility context: no formal WCAG target was provided for Slice-1; accessibility improvements should not block the pilot unless later mandated.

## Functional Requirements
- FR-01: The system shall allow authenticated users to upload PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG files up to 20 MB and immediately create a tracked document record with a unique document identifier.
- FR-02: The system shall persist the original uploaded file in profile-approved object storage and persist document metadata in PostgreSQL.
- FR-03: The system shall asynchronously parse, OCR where needed, classify, and extract key pilot-scope fields from uploaded documents.
- FR-04: The system shall store a confidence score for each extracted field and expose that score in the operator validation workspace.
- FR-05: The system shall preserve extracted text, document metadata, and lifecycle history for each document in the archive.
- FR-06: The validation workspace shall show document preview, extracted fields, confidence scores, workflow state, and guided correction controls in one operator-facing workspace.
- FR-07: No document shall transition to the Validated state without explicit human confirmation.
- FR-08: Manual correction shall preserve original value, corrected value, actor, and timestamp.
- FR-09: The minimal workflow shall create an assignable validation task after processing and shall support the document lifecycle states Uploaded, Processing, ValidationReady, InValidation, Validated, and Exception.
- FR-10: Transition to validation-ready shall create a dashboard notification and may also send an email notification when email delivery is configured.
- FR-11: If parsing, OCR, or extraction fails, the document shall enter an operator-visible Exception state with a readable reason.
- FR-12: Authorized users shall be able to search by metadata and full text, open preview, and download the original file under RBAC.
- FR-13: Authorized users shall be able to initiate export jobs for permitted document sets or document artifacts, and exports shall be auditable.
- FR-14: The system shall provide generative summary and Q&A only for validated documents, with citations to supporting passages.
- FR-15: AI responses shall not modify metadata, lifecycle state, task state, or document content without explicit user action outside the AI response.
- FR-16: The system shall record audit events for upload, processing outcomes, corrections, validation, export, download, and AI query access where applicable.
- FR-17: Business APIs and operator-visible behavior shall remain unchanged across AWS and on-prem deployment profiles; profile differences are allowed only behind adapter contracts for storage, messaging, secrets, observability, runtime platform, and GPU serving.

## Non-Functional Requirements
- Performance: P95 upload acknowledgment shall be below 5 seconds for files up to 20 MB.
- Performance: P95 metadata/full-text search shall be below 2 seconds.
- Performance: P95 generative answer latency shall be at or below 20 seconds for one validated document up to 20 pages.
- Throughput: The system shall support 600 documents per month in phase 1 with burst handling around 50 documents per day.
- Availability: The pilot target shall be 99.5% during working hours.
- Recovery: Backup and recovery shall support RPO of 60 minutes and RTO of 240 minutes.
- Security: Authentication shall use OIDC and/or SAML, with MFA policy externalized to the IdP.
- Authorization: RBAC shall be enforced consistently across UI, API, search, export, and AI access.
- Data protection: Encryption at rest and in transit shall be enabled; logs shall redact PII and confidential document content.
- Data residency: Pilot and AI processing shall remain EU-resident.
- Data lifecycle: Transactional data retention baseline shall be 3,650 days; logs retention baseline shall be 180 days.
- Observability: Structured logs, OpenTelemetry traces, and Prometheus-compatible metrics shall cover ingest, OCR, workflow, search, export, and AI paths.
- Portability: AWS and on-prem profiles shall preserve the same business contracts, state semantics, and audit semantics.
- Quality gates: CI/CD shall enforce tests, lint, types, security, and build checks, with zero critical vulnerabilities on the default eval profile.

## High-Level Architecture
- The business layer is profile-independent and contains the Next.js operator UI, FastAPI business API, workflow/task logic, audit logic, and AI access control.
- Paperless-ngx provides the document core, while custom services handle validation workflow, audit, export, and validated-only AI guardrails.
- Infrastructure-specific behavior is isolated behind adapters for object storage, queue/event transport, secret provider, observability sink, and AI runtime.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[Operator] --> UI[Next.js Web App]
  IDP[OIDC/SAML IdP] --> UI
  UI --> API[FastAPI Business API]
  API --> CORE[Paperless-ngx Document Core]
  API --> WF[Workflow & Task Logic]
  API --> SEARCH[Search & Archive API]
  API --> AI[Validated-only RAG API]
  CORE --> WORKERS[OCR / Parsing / Classification Workers]
  WF --> NOTIF[Dashboard / Email Notification Service]
  API --> DB[(PostgreSQL 16)]
  API --> CACHE[(Redis-compatible Cache)]
  WORKERS --> DB
  WORKERS --> OBJ[(S3-compatible Object Storage)]
  AI --> DB
  AI --> VEC[(pgvector on PostgreSQL)]
  API --> ADAPT[Profile Adapter Layer]
  WORKERS --> ADAPT
  AI --> ADAPT
  ADAPT --> AWS[AWS Profile: S3 / SQS / SNS / Secrets / CloudWatch / GPU]
  ADAPT --> ONP[On-prem Profile: S3-compatible / Approved Queue/Event / Vault / Central Logs / GPU]
```

## Interfaces
- Web interface: desktop-first Italian UI for upload, validation inbox, task handling, archive search, preview, export initiation, and validated-only AI query.
- Business API: profile-independent REST resources for documents, extracted fields, tasks, notifications, search, exports, and AI queries.
- Event interface: asynchronous document-processing and task/notification events routed through the deployment-profile adapter.
- Identity interface: OIDC and/or SAML integration with external IdP; application groups or IdP groups provide RBAC inputs.
- Notification interface: dashboard notifications are mandatory; SMTP/email notifications are optional when configured.
- Storage interface: S3-compatible object storage adapter for original files and derived artifacts.
- AI interface: self-hosted inference only, accessed through a service boundary that enforces validated-only retrieval, citations, and no prompt logging.

## Data Model (logical)
### Entity: User
- id: UUID — primary key
- idp_subject: string — unique external identity reference
- display_name: string — operator-visible name
- email: string — notification target when enabled
- locale: string — defaults to Italian for pilot users
- role_set: string[] — RBAC groups from application and/or IdP
- is_active: boolean — soft-activation flag

### Entity: Document
- id: UUID — primary key and unique document identifier
- source_filename: string — original client filename
- input_format: enum — pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, jpg, png
- mime_type: string — detected media type
- size_bytes: integer — max 20 MB in Slice-1
- storage_key_original: string — object storage location for original file
- storage_key_text: string|null — location of extracted/OCR text when available
- classification_label: string|null — pilot taxonomy output
- lifecycle_state: enum — Uploaded, Processing, ValidationReady, InValidation, Validated, Exception
- exception_reason: string|null — readable reason for failures
- uploaded_by_user_id: UUID — FK to User
- uploaded_at: timestamp — creation time
- validated_by_user_id: UUID|null — FK to User
- validated_at: timestamp|null — explicit human validation time

### Entity: ExtractedField
- id: UUID — primary key
- document_id: UUID — FK to Document
- field_name: string — pilot-scope metadata key
- proposed_value: string|null — system-suggested value
- final_value: string|null — user-confirmed value
- confidence_score: decimal — range 0.00 to 1.00
- provenance_ref: string|null — source reference or span locator
- corrected_by_user_id: UUID|null — FK to User
- corrected_at: timestamp|null — correction time

### Entity: ValidationTask
- id: UUID — primary key
- document_id: UUID — FK to Document
- assignee_user_id: UUID|null — FK to User
- task_state: enum — Open, InProgress, Completed, Cancelled
- created_at: timestamp — task creation time
- opened_at: timestamp|null — first operator open time
- completed_at: timestamp|null — completion time
- completion_outcome: string|null — validated, exception-confirmed, or other configured outcome

### Entity: Notification
- id: UUID — primary key
- user_id: UUID — FK to User
- document_id: UUID|null — FK to Document when document-related
- channel: enum — Dashboard, Email
- notification_type: string — task assigned, validation ready, exception, export ready
- delivery_state: enum — Pending, Sent, Read, Failed
- created_at: timestamp — enqueue time
- sent_at: timestamp|null — delivery time
- read_at: timestamp|null — dashboard read time

### Entity: ExportJob
- id: UUID — primary key
- requested_by_user_id: UUID — FK to User
- document_id: UUID|null — FK to Document for single-document export
- scope_json: json — export filter or scope definition
- output_format: string — configured export type
- job_state: enum — Requested, Running, Completed, Failed
- artifact_key: string|null — output artifact location
- requested_at: timestamp — request time
- completed_at: timestamp|null — finish time

### Entity: AuditEvent
- id: UUID — primary key
- document_id: UUID|null — FK to Document when applicable
- actor_type: enum — User, Service

- before_state: string|null — prior lifecycle/task/value state

### Entity: AIQuery

- document_id: UUID — FK to Document
- requested_by_user_id: UUID — FK to User
- query_hash: string — non-reversible or approved hashed query fingerprint
- citation_count: integer — number of returned citations
- response_status: enum — Allowed, Denied, Failed
- latency_ms: integer — end-to-end response latency
- created_at: timestamp — access time

## Key Workflows
- Intake to validation: upload creates a document record, asynchronous processing extracts data, a validation task is created, the operator corrects fields if needed, and explicit validation closes the task.
- Exception handling: any processing failure moves the document to Exception with a readable reason and visible operator follow-up.
- Search and export: authorized users search by metadata or full text, preview or download documents, and request auditable export jobs.
- AI query: only validated documents are eligible; the response must include citations and must not change business state.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Operator
  participant UI as Web App
  participant API as Business API
  participant Q as Queue Adapter
  participant W as OCR/IDP Worker
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  participant N as Notification Service

  O->>UI: Upload document
  UI->>API: Create tracked document
  API->>DB: Save metadata (Uploaded)
  API->>Q: Enqueue processing
  API-->>O: Return document ID + acknowledgement
  Q->>W: Process document
  W->>DB: Save text, classification, extracted fields
  alt Processing success
    W->>DB: Set state = ValidationReady
    W->>DB: Create ValidationTask
    W->>N: Emit dashboard/email notification
    O->>UI: Open validation task
    UI->>API: Submit corrections
    API->>DB: Save corrected fields + audit
    O->>UI: Confirm validation
    UI->>API: Validate document
    API->>DB: Set state = Validated, close task, write audit
  else Processing failure
    W->>DB: Set state = Exception with readable reason
    W->>N: Notify operator
  end
```

## Security & Compliance
- GDPR is mandatory for Slice-1.
- User authentication shall integrate with OIDC and/or SAML; MFA policy is enforced by the external IdP, not hard-coded in the application.
- Authorization shall use RBAC sourced from application groups or IdP groups and shall apply consistently to upload, validation, search, export, download, and AI query access.
- Encryption at rest and encryption in transit shall be enabled across all deployment profiles.
- The platform shall treat business data as confidential and apply data minimization and PII redaction in logs.
- Prompt logging shall remain disabled; any AI-related persisted evidence must be redacted and must not contain raw prompts with personal or confidential data.
- Validated-only AI access is a hard guardrail; non-validated documents must not be answerable through the generative interface.
- Auditability must support reconstruction of who uploaded, corrected, validated, exported, downloaded, or queried a document.
- EU-resident deployment is required for pilot data and self-hosted AI inference.

## Deployment & Operations
- Deployment profiles: dev, uat, and prod.
- AWS pilot profile: containerized Linux services on AWS ECS Fargate with S3, SQS, SNS, AWS Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus-compatible metrics, and AWS GPU runtime for AI where used.
- On-prem profile: containerized services on approved on-prem containers or Kubernetes with PostgreSQL, Redis-compatible cache, S3-compatible object storage, approved queue/event transport, Vault or approved secret store, centralized log sink, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus-compatible metrics, and approved GPU runtime.
- The same business services, APIs, lifecycle states, and RBAC behavior shall be deployed in both profiles; only adapter bindings and configuration may differ.
- Alembic shall manage database migrations.
- Backup and recovery operations shall meet RPO 60 minutes and RTO 240 minutes.
- Internet egress shall remain restricted to approved internal services and approved regional infrastructure services.
- CI/CD shall run through GitHub Actions workflows for CI and CD, with branch protection requiring PRs, at least one review, status checks, and Trivy security scanning.
- Operational telemetry shall include structured logs, traces, and metrics for ingest, OCR, workflow, search, export, and AI paths.

## Risks & Mitigations
- OCR and extraction quality may vary by document quality and layout — mitigate with real sample documents, confidence scoring, provenance display, and operator correction flow.
- Business logic may drift toward AWS-specific services — mitigate by enforcing adapter contracts and parity testing from the start.
- The 2-week pilot window is tight — mitigate by keeping one validation-oriented workflow only and excluding third-party integrations and backfile ingestion.
- Operators may distrust AI suggestions — mitigate with clear confidence scores, side-by-side preview, provenance, and explicit human validation gates.
- Retention rules and sensitive document classes are not fully confirmed — mitigate with DPO/compliance review before go-live and baseline retention only for pilot.
- AI can produce unhelpful or unsupported answers — mitigate with validated-only retrieval, citations, self-hosted approved models, and no autonomous state changes.

## Assumptions
- Real sample documents are available for PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, and scanned inputs during Slice-1.
- An AWS account in an EU region is available for the pilot, and an approved on-prem target environment is available for parity validation.
- An email/SMTP channel exists or can be responsibly mocked for the pilot.
- An enterprise IdP exists, or Keycloak is approved as the identity provider for pilot use.
- Pilot document categories and key fields will be limited to a scope that is achievable within the 2-week window and sufficient to test the 85% extraction target.
- Formal accessibility requirements beyond the stated desktop-first baseline are not blocking for Slice-1.
- No reusable canonical application entrypoints or shared auth/config modules were evidenced in the provided local snapshot.
- Implementation decisions were informed by the local source snapshot and project artifacts provided for this run.

## Success Metrics
- TTFA from login to first validated document is 10 minutes or less.
- Task success for upload → validation → search flows is at least 85% without assistance.
- Critical error rate is 2% or less per ingest or validation operation.
- First-pass extraction accuracy on key fields is at least 85%.
- Search-to-open time is 30 seconds or less in 90% of cases.
- Average validation time is at or below 2 minutes per document.
- Idea-to-demo lead time is 10 calendar days or less.
- Pilot satisfaction is at or above 4.2/5 across the initial user group.

## Acceptance Criteria

# SPEC — docuZen a Zen 2030 Document Management & Workflow

## Summary
- docuZen Slice-1 is a desktop-first, Italian-language document management and workflow platform for 5 named users, targeting up to 20 GB and 600 documents per month in phase 1.
- The slice must support upload of PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG; OCR/IDP; human validation; minimal task workflow; archive search; controlled export; and validated-only generative summary/Q&A.
- AWS in an EU region is the primary pilot delivery profile, but on-prem is a supported equivalent profile with the same business APIs, lifecycle semantics, RBAC semantics, audit semantics, and operator-visible workflow behavior.
- The solution is open-source-core and must avoid dependency on commercial DMS application packages as the primary slice-1 application core.
- The authoritative implementation baseline is Next.js 14 + FastAPI + Paperless-ngx, with PostgreSQL 16, Redis-compatible cache, S3-compatible object storage, profile-driven messaging, and self-hosted AI/RAG components.

## Goals
- Reduce manual data entry by at least 50% per in-scope document.
- Achieve at least 85% first-pass extraction accuracy on key pilot-scope fields.
- Ensure every document can be uploaded, processed, reviewed, explicitly validated by a human, and archived with a complete audit trail.
- Enable metadata and full-text retrieval so that archived documents can be searched and opened within 30 seconds in 90% of cases.
- Provide a simple operator workflow with one main upload path, one validation-oriented workflow, task visibility, and dashboard/email notifications.
- Provide validated-only generative summary and Q&A with citations and no autonomous business action.
- Preserve functional parity across AWS and on-prem deployment profiles by isolating profile-specific infrastructure behind adapter contracts.

## Non-Goals
- Replacing ERP, accounting, CRM, PEC, or HR systems.
- Implementing full accounting approval, payment automation, or end-to-end finance workflows.
- Building a generic ECM platform before pilot value is proven.
- Optimizing for extreme enterprise-scale workloads beyond pilot targets.
- Allowing AI to change metadata, lifecycle state, or business outcomes without explicit human action.

## Users & Context
- Primary user: administrative or document operator working in a desktop-first back-office web application.
- Secondary stakeholders: IT for platform/access, Finance or Administration for controls/audit, DPO and Compliance for personal data and retention, HR as a future extension.
- Operating context: Italian-language web UI, 5 named users, up to 7,200 documents per year at pilot baseline, notifications via dashboard and email.
- Supported inputs for Slice-1: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG.
- Accessibility context: no formal WCAG target was provided for Slice-1; accessibility improvements should not block the pilot unless later mandated.

## Functional Requirements
- FR-01: The system shall allow authenticated users to upload PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, JPG, and PNG files up to 20 MB and immediately create a tracked document record with a unique document identifier.
- FR-02: The system shall persist the original uploaded file in profile-approved object storage and persist document metadata in PostgreSQL.
- FR-03: The system shall asynchronously parse, OCR where needed, classify, and extract key pilot-scope fields from uploaded documents.
- FR-04: The system shall store a confidence score for each extracted field and expose that score in the operator validation workspace.
- FR-05: The system shall preserve extracted text, document metadata, and lifecycle history for each document in the archive.
- FR-06: The validation workspace shall show document preview, extracted fields, confidence scores, workflow state, and guided correction controls in one operator-facing workspace.
- FR-07: No document shall transition to the Validated state without explicit human confirmation.
- FR-08: Manual correction shall preserve original value, corrected value, actor, and timestamp.
- FR-09: The minimal workflow shall create an assignable validation task after processing and shall support the document lifecycle states Uploaded, Processing, ValidationReady, InValidation, Validated, and Exception.
- FR-10: Transition to validation-ready shall create a dashboard notification and may also send an email notification when email delivery is configured.
- FR-11: If parsing, OCR, or extraction fails, the document shall enter an operator-visible Exception state with a readable reason.
- FR-12: Authorized users shall be able to search by metadata and full text, open preview, and download the original file under RBAC.
- FR-13: Authorized users shall be able to initiate export jobs for permitted document sets or document artifacts, and exports shall be auditable.
- FR-14: The system shall provide generative summary and Q&A only for validated documents, with citations to supporting passages.
- FR-15: AI responses shall not modify metadata, lifecycle state, task state, or document content without explicit user action outside the AI response.
- FR-16: The system shall record audit events for upload, processing outcomes, corrections, validation, export, download, and AI query access where applicable.
- FR-17: Business APIs and operator-visible behavior shall remain unchanged across AWS and on-prem deployment profiles; profile differences are allowed only behind adapter contracts for storage, messaging, secrets, observability, runtime platform, and GPU serving.

## Non-Functional Requirements
- Performance: P95 upload acknowledgment shall be below 5 seconds for files up to 20 MB.
- Performance: P95 metadata/full-text search shall be below 2 seconds.
- Performance: P95 generative answer latency shall be at or below 20 seconds for one validated document up to 20 pages.
- Throughput: The system shall support 600 documents per month in phase 1 with burst handling around 50 documents per day.
- Availability: The pilot target shall be 99.5% during working hours.
- Recovery: Backup and recovery shall support RPO of 60 minutes and RTO of 240 minutes.
- Security: Authentication shall use OIDC and/or SAML, with MFA policy externalized to the IdP.
- Authorization: RBAC shall be enforced consistently across UI, API, search, export, and AI access.
- Data protection: Encryption at rest and in transit shall be enabled; logs shall redact PII and confidential document content.
- Data residency: Pilot and AI processing shall remain EU-resident.
- Data lifecycle: Transactional data retention baseline shall be 3,650 days; logs retention baseline shall be 180 days.
- Observability: Structured logs, OpenTelemetry traces, and Prometheus-compatible metrics shall cover ingest, OCR, workflow, search, export, and AI paths.
- Portability: AWS and on-prem profiles shall preserve the same business contracts, state semantics, and audit semantics.
- Quality gates: CI/CD shall enforce tests, lint, types, security, and build checks, with zero critical vulnerabilities on the default eval profile.

## High-Level Architecture
- The business layer is profile-independent and contains the Next.js operator UI, FastAPI business API, workflow/task logic, audit logic, and AI access control.
- Paperless-ngx provides the document core, while custom services handle validation workflow, audit, export, and validated-only AI guardrails.
- Infrastructure-specific behavior is isolated behind adapters for object storage, queue/event transport, secret provider, observability sink, and AI runtime.

  API --> CORE[Paperless-ngx Document Core]
  API --> WF[Workflow & Task Logic]
  API --> SEARCH[Search & Archive API]
  API --> AI[Validated-only RAG API]
  CORE --> WORKERS[OCR / Parsing / Classification Workers]

  AI --> DB

  WORKERS --> ADAPT
  AI --> ADAPT

- size_bytes: integer — max 20 MB in Slice-1

- storage_key_text: string|null — location of extracted/OCR text when available
- classification_label: string|null — pilot taxonomy output
- lifecycle_state: enum — Uploaded, Processing, ValidationReady, InValidation, Validated, Exception
- exception_reason: string|null — readable reason for failures
- uploaded_by_user_id: UUID — FK to User
- uploaded_at: timestamp — creation time
- validated_by_user_id: UUID|null — FK to User
- validated_at: timestamp|null — explicit human validation time

### Entity: ExtractedField
- id: UUID — primary key
- document_id: UUID — FK to Document
- field_name: string — pilot-scope metadata key
- proposed_value: string|null — system-suggested value
- final_value: string|null — user-confirmed value
- confidence_score: decimal — range 0.00 to 1.00
- provenance_ref: string|null — source reference or span locator
- corrected_by_user_id: UUID|null — FK to User
- corrected_at: timestamp|null — correction time

### Entity: ValidationTask

- document_id: UUID — FK to Document
- assignee_user_id: UUID|null — FK to User
- task_state: enum — Open, InProgress, Completed, Cancelled

- requested_by_user_id: UUID — FK to User
